data.intro: I'm Nathan Nixon. I run Nixon Creative Studio from Cincinnati, Ohio, and I plan, design and build every site myself. When a project needs photographs, I take those too. You deal with me from the first conversation to launch day, and after it.
data.thesis_accent: churches, schools, nonprofits and small businesses

data.story_heading: I came to this work through a camera.
data.story_sub: From Edinburgh to Cincinnati, and from portraits to websites.

children.text: For years I photographed portraits, families and weddings, the days people most want to remember. The part I loved was helping someone show up at their best.

When the shoots dried up in 2020, I started building websites for a few of those same clients. It turned out to be the same job in a new medium: work out what someone is really trying to say, then make it clear.

Before any of that I studied mechanical engineering at the University of Edinburgh, back home in Scotland. It taught me to take a thing apart, understand why each piece is there, and put it back together so it holds. I build websites the same way: structure first, surface second, and set up so the person who inherits the site can keep it running.

I'm also on the volunteer media team at Crestview Presbyterian Church. I run the weekly livestream, plan and buy the equipment upgrades, and shoot the photos and video the church uses on its website and its socials.
Web design is the studio's main work now, but the photographer's eye stayed. When a project needs photographs, I take them myself.
I moved from Scotland to Cincinnati in 2017 to be with my wife, and became a US citizen in 2022. We are raising two kids here, and in 2026 we bought our first house.
Away from a screen I'm usually out on a long run, chasing landscapes with a camera, deep in an ambitious Lego build with the kids, or a few episodes into a history drama.

data.principles_sub: Three things you can hold me to on every project.

principles.title: You work with me, start to finish
principles.body: The person who answers your first email is the person who plans, designs and builds your site. Nothing is passed to a subcontractor, and you never have to explain your organization twice.

principles.title: A plan we both sign off first
principles.body: Every project starts with a working session and a one-page brief we both agree on. The design follows from that brief, not from whichever template looks freshest.

principles.title: A site your own people can run
principles.body: I pick the platform that fits your budget and the people who will keep it up, from custom code to Squarespace or WordPress, then set it up so the next volunteer or staff member can keep it running after I hand it over.
